LoggerGlue

Source: R/Logger.R
LoggerGlue.Rd

LoggerGlue uses glue::glue() instead of base::sprintf() to construct log messages. glue is a very well designed package for string interpolation. It makes composing log messages more flexible and comfortable at the price of an additional dependency and slightly less performance than sprintf().

glue() lets you define temporary named variables inside the call. As with the normal Logger, these named arguments get turned into custom fields; however, you can suppress this behaviour by making named argument start with a ".". Please refer to vignette("lgr", package = "lgr") for examples.

Super classes

Filterable -> Logger -> LoggerGlue

Active bindings

transformer

NULL or a function. The .transformer passed to glue::glue() for string interpolation. See $set_transformer().

LoggerGlue$new()

Create a new LoggerGlue. As with Logger$new(), you should not normally call this directly but use get_logger_glue() instead.

Usage

LoggerGlue$new(
  name = "(unnamed logger)",
  appenders = list(),
  threshold = NULL,
  filters = list(),
  exception_handler = default_exception_handler,
  propagate = TRUE,
  replace_empty = "<NULL>",
  transformer = NULL
)

Arguments

name, appenders, threshold, filters, exception_handler, propagate

See section Active bindings.

replace_empty

The replacement value used for empty log message arguments (NULL or empty vectors). See $set_replace_empty().

transformer

NULL or a function with two arguments (text, envir) that is passed on to glue::glue() as its .transformer argument to customize string interpolation. See $set_transformer().

LoggerGlue$fatal()

Log an Event fatal priority using glue::glue() for string interpolation.

Usage

LoggerGlue$fatal(..., caller = get_caller(-8L), .envir = parent.frame())

Arguments

...

unnamed character fragments are glued together with glue::glue() to construct the log message; named arguments are turned into custom fields (a leading . in the name suppresses this). See the class description for details.

.envir

the environment in which glue() evaluates {expr} placeholders. See glue::glue().

msg, ..., caller

see $log()

LoggerGlue$log()

Log an event, constructing the message with glue::glue() instead of sprintf(). Unlike Logger$log(), there is no dedicated msg argument: unnamed fragments in ... are glued together to form the message, and named arguments are available to glue() as temporary variables (and become custom fields unless their name starts with .).

Usage

LoggerGlue$log(
  level,
  ...,
  timestamp = Sys.time(),
  caller = get_caller(-7),
  .envir = parent.frame()
)

Arguments

level

a character or integer scalar. See log_levels.

...

unnamed character fragments are glued together with glue::glue() to construct the log message; named arguments are turned into custom fields (a leading . in the name suppresses this).

timestamp

POSIXct. Timestamp of the event.

caller

a character scalar. The name of the calling function.

.envir

the environment in which glue() evaluates {expr} placeholders. See glue::glue().

LoggerGlue$list_log()

list_log() is a shortcut for do.call(LoggerGlue$log, x). Unlike Logger$list_log(), an element named msg in x is treated as an unnamed glue() fragment rather than a dedicated message argument.

Usage

LoggerGlue$list_log(x)

Arguments

x

a named list that must at least contain the named elements level and timestamp

LoggerGlue$spawn()

Spawn a child LoggerGlue. Equivalent to get_logger_glue(paste0(name, "/", child)).

Usage

LoggerGlue$spawn(name)

Arguments

name

character vector. Name of the child logger get_logger("foo/bar")$spawn("baz") is equivalent to get_logger("foo/bar/baz")

LoggerGlue$set_transformer()

Set the transformer for glue string interpolation

Usage

LoggerGlue$set_transformer(x)

Arguments

x

single function taking two arguments. See glue::glue().
